content.title: Michigan claims first men's basketball national championship since 1989: Recap
content.text: Updated April 6, 2026, 11:38 p.m. ETThere's one game remaining in the college basketball season, and it's for the national championship. Michigan and UConn have survived through five NCAA Tournament games and now meet for the title. Follow the action here with live updates throughout the game by Detroit News contributor Kameron Goodwill. Final: No. 1 Michigan 69, No. 2 UConn 63Hail to the victors indeed, as Michigan men's basketball finally ended theirs and the Big Ten's national championship drought on Monday night.It's the program's first title since 1989 and the first for the Big Ten since Michigan State won in 2000, as the conference that dominated throughout the tournament takes home the trophy. It wasn't as pretty or as dominant as their previous five games in the tournament, but it was a gritty win for a team that played like the best in the country.They needed this performance to defeat a UConn program that won two of the previous three national titles before tonight. Dusty May wins his first championship at Michigan in just his second year as head coach with a starting five full of transfers. Leading in scoring was Elliot Cadeau, who bounced back from a rough shooting performance in the Final Four game on Saturday with a game-high 19 points, along with being announced as the Final Four's Most Outstanding Player.Yaxel Lendeborg battled through a bad ankle and MCL to end with 13 points, and Trey McKenney ended with a clutch nine points off the bench, including a big 3-pointer with 1:51 remaining to give the Wolverines a nine-point lead. For one shining moment, Ann Arbor can celebrate as they regain their spot at the top of men's college basketball. Michigan holds on late rally, takes home second national championship in school history in close win over UConnThe ensuing inbound goes awry as Lendeborg turns it over under UConn's rim, then Ball steps back and banks home a 3-pointer over the contest of McKenney and now the lead is cut to four. Review confirms the shot as Gayle's fouled with 29.5 remaining, but he misses both free throws. UConn goes to the other end and Karaban is short on his 3-pointer and McKenney is fouled with 13.4 remaining.UConn challenges the call and loses, losing their final timeout as McKenney swishes home both free throws, then UConn can't hit another shot and the national championship returns to Ann Arbor! The Michigan Wolverines are your 2026 champions! Wolverines come up clutch at the free throw line, up 67-60 with less than a minute left in national championship gameReed again heads to the free throw line and makes both free throws, as UConn puts the pressure on the inbound but Michigan gets it across the line and Demery fouls out for UConn. Cadeau sinks both as Michigan's hit 20 straight free throws now, but Karaban hits both shots at the line as UConn's still in it. A tie-up on the inbound gives Michigan possession as they call timeout with 48 seconds left. UConn gets closer, McKenney slams the door with 3-pointer as Michigan's up nine lateReed heads to the line after the timeout and hits both free throws, but after a McKenney miss, Mullins is called for an offensive foul on Cadeau. Cadeau draws the foul and hits both free throws, but Karaban hits a big three to cut the deficit to six points. Gayle gets the ball stolen by Reed but UConn can't cut into the lead, then on the other end McKenney steps back and hits a big 3-pointer as it's a nine-point lead again! 1:49 left and the Wolverines can almost taste the victory. Michigan holds onto lead, minutes away from national championship win over UConnMichigan continues to stay aggressive despite the poor shooting, as McKenney draws the foul and hits both free throws. Karaban misses both free throws, then Demary misses a three. Lendeborg hits the layup on the other end, but UConn hits their first three of the second half thanks to Mullins as they call a quick timeout with 5:21 left.Michigan leads, 56-48, out of the timeout, as Lendeborg can't hit the floater but tips in his own miss for a 10-point Wolverine lead. Mullins hits his second straight three for an answer, but Lendeborg draws the foul and hits both free throws. Timeout is called with 3:48 left and Michigan's up by nine points. UConn cuts into deficit, but Wolverines are holding on, leading 52-45 with over seven minutes remainingJohnson gets a big block on Ross but fouls him on the follow-through, as Ross hits both free throws and UConn is down by nine points now. Johnson gets a clean block the next time down on Mullins as another quick timeout is taken with 11:33 left. After the timeout, things get a little physical as Cadeau takes a hard fall after a miss but gets up quickly. A few seconds later, Johnson and Silas Demary Jr. get tied up and fall near the sideline.It's a defensive struggle again, as UConn gets a steal but it's Lendeborg with the big block on Ross, then Johnson follows up McKenney's miss with a tip-in layup. More blocks as Johnson pins Mullins' shot at the rum, but UConn ends the drought with a Karaban layup. Demery hits the layup a few moments later and the lead is cut to five, but Gayle lobs it up to Mara in transition to end the Husky run. Timeout taken with 7:16 left as the Wolverines inch closer to a huge victory. Cadeau's 3-pointer helps Wolverines take largest lead of the night, up 48-37 over UConn with 12:47 leftAfter the timeout, it seems that both offenses have finally woken up. Lendeborg hits his free throw, then both teams trade buckets, ending Cadeau hits a deep three! It's the first one for the Wolverines all night with 12:47 left in the second half, and Michigan's now up by 11 points and UConn needs a timeout. Michigan begins to extend lead, take 40-33 lead over UConn early in second halfWolverines get a stop to start the second half, as Mara throws a perfect outlet pass to Burnett as Burnett's fouled in transition and hits both free throws. Both teams trade turnovers and continue to struggle putting the ball in the hoop, but Cadeau drives hard and hits the layup plus the foul! It's Solo Ball's fourth foul as he heads to the bench, and Cadeau hits the free throw to extend the Wolverines' lead.Braylon Mullins scoops inside for a put-back layup, but Lendeborg rumbles and hits his own and-one layup, as he'll go to the line after the timeout. Halftime: No. 1 Michigan 33, No. 2 UConn 29The national championship game has turned into one of attrition, as the Wolverines hold a slim lead to the Huskies as halftime hits.While Michigan's gone over the 90-point threshold through the entire tournament, they may be lucky to get over 70 points the way this first half has gone. Playing at a pace that suits UConn, both teams have shot under 40% from the field and the Wolverines haven't made any of their eight 3-point attempts, while UConn has gone 5-for-15 from deep.But again, Michigan's getting to the free throw line and is 11-for-12 from the line. Morez Johnson Jr. is leading the Wolverines with 10 points in the first half, while Yaxel Lendeborg is 1-for-5 from the field with just four points so far. Alex Karaban and Solo Ball are UConn's leading scorer with eight points each, as both players have hit two 3-pointers. Michigan enters halftime with 33-29 lead over UConn in national championship gameThe timeout worked as Ball cashes in a long 3-pointer, but Mara hooks in a shot as the lead is now at three points for Michigan. Both offenses continue to struggle putting the ball in the hoop, but Gayle flies in for a loud putback dunk with under 30 seconds left! Reed is fouled on a layup attempt with under three seconds remaining, but he splits the free throws and Cadeau can't draw the foul on a long 3-point attempt and we head to halftime of this low-scoring fight. Wolverines go on 6-0 scoring run to take 29-25 lead over UConn with less than three minutes left in first halfKaraban is called for a flagrant foul, as Johnson hits two free throws and gives Michigan the ball back, leading to a Lendeborg layup for his first field goal of the night. A defensive stop leads to a Mara layup as the Wolverines take the lead and UConn calls their first timeout. Michigan takes advantage of free throws, UConn still holds lead, up 25-23UConn has slowed the pace of this game down to their own in this low-scoring first half. But they've built up fouls, putting Michigan in 1-and-1 territory with under seven minutes left as Nimari Burnett and Yaxel Lendeborg gets on the board with free throws. Roddy Gayle Jr. hits both his free throws, then Mara is called for goaltending on former Wolverine Tarris Reed Jr. as UConn takes a two-point lead with less than four minutes remaining in the first half. Wolverines' offense slows down, UConn takes slim lead late in first halfRoss splits the free throws to tie the game, then Karaban hits a corner-3 to give UConn their first lead of the night at 16-13. A Malachi Smith layup gives the Huskies a three-point lead, but Trey McKenney finds Aday Mara inside for the layup and a third Wolverine enters the scoring sheet. UConn leads, 18-17, with seven minutes remaining in the first half. Johnson, Cadeau carrying Michigan's offense, Wolverines up, 11-10, over Huskies in first halfSolo Ball, the Huskie dealing with his own injury, hits a three to have five points, but Cadeau answers with an and-one layup over Silas Demary Jr. for his second foul. Cadeau misses the free throw, then Elite Eight hero Alex Karaban hits his first three as UConn cuts the deficit to 11-10. Cadeau fouls Jayden Ross on a layup and that will take us to another timeout with 11:57 left in the first half.Wolverines strike first, take 9-4 lead over Huskies early in national championship gameIt's Michigan and UConn fighting for the NCAA national championship here in Indianapolis and we are underway! Morez Johnson Jr. gets the Wolverines their first bucket with a layup, then Elliot Cadeau is fouled while shooting a 3-pointer and hits all three free throws to make it a 7-2 lead for Michigan. A Roddy Gayle Jr. block sends us to our first TV timeout as Michigan holds a 9-4 lead early in this national championship game.
